newsitem.title: USA: Alternative Living, Sterling to merge.
newsitem.headline: Alternative Living, Sterling to merge.

text.p: Alternative Living Services Inc said Thursday it entered into a definitive merger agreement with Sterling House Corp.
Alternative Living said it would issue 1.1 shares of its common stock in exchange for each outstanding share of Sterling House common stock in the pooling of interests transaction.

"This strategic business combination will create the nation's largest assisted living company providing healthcare services both in terms of total revenues and residences in operation, as well as the largest operator of residences for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and other memory impairments," Assisted Living said.

The combined company will have 178 residences in operation in 19 states with capacity to accommodate about 8,000 residents. The combined company will have 65 residences under construction and 81 in development. Annualized revenues of the combined company exceeed $115 million, the company said.

The boards of directors of both companies have unanimously approved the merger agreement. The transaction is valued at about $170 million, including assumption of all outstanding Sterling House indebtedness, the company said.
After the merger, there will be about 18.5 million shares of Assisted Living common stock outstanding with a value, based on current prices, of about $400 million, it said.
Holders of about 46 percent of the outstanding shares of Sterling House have agreed to vote their shares in favor of the merger, the company said.
Assisted and Sterling have granted each other options to buy 19.9 percent of the outstanding common stock of the other company under certain circumstances.
The merger is intended to qualify as a tax-free reorganization and is expected to be accounted for as a pooling of interests, Assisted Living said.
Closing of the merger is expected in the fourth quarter of 1997, the company said.

Alternative Living is among the nation's largest operators of assisted living residences. It offers four types of home-like residential models, including the Clare Bridge residence for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias; and three models to serve the frail elderly.
